notes: Persuade and Intimidate on an NPC from its radial menu in exploration (designer request 2026-10-12). The rolls are the combat ones (combat/actions.json tasks persuade, intimidate and resistRequest): Persuade is Presence + Command, Intimidate is Control + Security, and the NPC resists with Control + Command. These pairings are Prototype picks: the book deliberately sets none for social actions (Core p.280 sidebar).

Book (Core p.280, as recorded in combat/actions.json): a resisted request is an opposed task. The asker rolls first and its successes, less its own Difficulty changes (p.256), set the resister's Difficulty; the resister then rolls. No successes: nothing was asked that needs resisting (counted here as a loss). Book p.256: the side that sets the Difficulty generates 1 Momentum per success the other side fell short (to the group pool); the NPC's Momentum when it resists goes to Threat, as in combat (p.265).

Designer decisions (2026-10-12), effects on the NPC's disposition (dispositionOrder, awareness.json) and on the Task Checks in its conversation: Persuade win: persuadeWinSteps friendlier, and its conversation checks get conversationDifficulty.persuadeWin (implementer recommendation, awaiting approval: easier rather than skipped, so Intimidate stays the way to skip them). Persuade loss: nothing changes. Intimidate win: an NPC that would fight stands down (neutral, never joins a fight), otherwise intimidateWinSteps friendlier; it is Intimidated: its conversation's Task Checks pass without a roll (every check, technical ones included; designer decision 2026-10-14), and it resists later requests at +intimidatedDifficulty. Intimidate loss: intimidateLossSteps more hostile, alerted to the asker, no longer Intimidated, and its conversation checks get conversationDifficulty.intimidateLoss; an NPC already at the hostile end (aggressive) attacks (designer decision 2026-10-14). Intimidated does not carry into a fight (designer decision 2026-10-14). The NPC's Momentum when it resists becomes Threat in exploration too (designer decision 2026-10-14).

Book support for those effects (Core pp.279-282): a resisted request can't be made again unchanged (p.279; the Prototype uses a cooldown instead). Evidence lowers a Persuade task's Difficulty by 1 (p.281), the precedent for Persuade making checks easier. Successful Intimidation imposes a trait representing fear (p.282; the Prototype's Intimidated). Failed Intimidation makes further attempts in the scene harder, and Intimidation is inherently hostile: it can worsen other interactions, cause lingering resentment, or provoke a target to aggression (p.282; the Prototype's angrier NPC, harder checks and an aggressive NPC attacking). Prototype only, not in the book: disposition steps, skipping conversation checks, the cooldown, and the conversationDifficulty limits.
conversationDifficulty: the running total of those changes is kept between min and max and added to every Task Check in that NPC's conversation (never below Difficulty 0).

Prototype: only an NPC that is up, not friendly, has a character to roll for, and is within earshot (combat/actions.json communication audibleRangeTiles) can be asked. cooldownSeconds (designer decision 2026-10-14: 10, in place of the book's no-repeat rule): world seconds before the same character can Persuade or Intimidate again (shared by both).
